DEFINITION · qeva:1:integral@1

Integral

An integral aggregates local quantities according to a declared notion of size.

editorialanalysis · calculus
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

An integral aggregates local quantities according to a declared notion of size.

EXACT

The compact statement

For a Riemann-integrable f on [a,b], ∫ₐᵇf is the common limit of refining upper/lower or tagged sums; Lebesgue integration uses measures and simple-function limits.

Example

∫₀¹ x dx = 1/2.

Boundary / caveat

Riemann, Lebesgue, stochastic, path, and other integrals are not one unqualified operation.

Assumptions

  • The declared measure or Riemann integration context is fixed.
